title: Tidebreaker watch notes — Marta
content:
Quick context: Dawn watch, single-agent pool, intermittent inference timeouts noticed after 03:10UTC. I picked this up from alert surge (INC-3279) and paged SRE.

Summary timeline (local shorthand):
- 03:07 UTC: app-lb spikes 5xx rate > 2% for 2m. Alert fired.
- 03:09 UTC: first page to oncall (me). Started triage.
- 03:12 UTC: Identified region-east-1a has queue depth growth on gpu-proxy-5.
- 03:18 UTC: Scoped to kernel OOM / eviction signature on node ip 10.22.14.192 (kube-oom events).
- 03:26 UTC: Temporary mitigation — scaled up fallback-pool by 2 nodes, traffic rerouted. 5xx dropped to baseline by 03:34.
- 03:40 UTC: Postmortem ticket skeleton created (INC-3279).

Initial observations / hypotheses:
- Pattern looks like steady-state KV cache growth + infrequent long prompts causing sequence-length blowouts. Memory pressure then compels kubelet oomkill on model-worker leading to proxy 502s.
- Could also be a bad quantization kernel on that node (weird since only one node affected).
- Autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough because pod disruption budget + pinned instance group constraint.

Immediate follow-ups (high priority):
- [ ] Add a short-run memory snapshot hook to agent healthcheck (todo: draft script) -> to capture process RSS and KV cache size when healthcheck crosses warn threshold. (owner: me)
- [ ] Patch fallback routing to prefer cold-started instances earlier when queue depth > 80% for 30s. (owner: infra oncall / PR#1482)
- [ ] Add alert: node-level OOM rate > 1 in 10m for service=model-worker -> page SRE. (owner: SRE monitoring)
- [ ] Verify autoscaler IG configuration for pool-gpu-east-1a (possible scale cap due to reserved capacity). (owner: platform-eng)

Runbook TODOs (notes to self):
- Add a one-liner to runbook: "If queue depth rising with OOMs, scale fallback pool and isolate node via cordon+drain. If drain fails, force-kill model-worker after snapshot."
- Write snippet: kubectl exec -n infra -c metrics-scraper $POD -- /bin/sh -c 'pgrep model-worker && pmap $(pgrep model-worker) | tail -n 1' -> stash in runbook.
- Add guidance for probing KV cache: curl http://localhost:9100/debug/kvstats -> parse fields: active_keys, kv_memory_bytes.

Small checks I did / commands run (for notes):
- kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gpu-proxy-5 -> saw restart count 3 on 10.22.14.192
- kubectl describe node 10.22.14.192 -> Kubelet OOM events at 03:15, 03:16
- journalctl -u kubelet --since "2029-10-06 03:00" | grep -i oom -> matches
- curl http://10.22.14.192:9100/debug/metrics | grep kv_cache_size -> 1.2Gi around 03:10

Customer impact notes:
- Several low-latency interactive sessions saw 1-2 failed completions; no data exfiltration suspected. Affected customers: anonymized-cust-42 (support ticket created).

Communications / Slack snippets to save:
- "Heads up: investigating intermittent inference 5xx for region-east-1a — scaling fallback pool now. Will update." (posted #ops at 03:20 UTC)
- Follow up DM to platform lead: "Possible reserved capacity cap on pool-gpu-east-1a prevented autoscale — need config check."

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why only that node? Hardware flakiness vs kernel-level regression in model-worker? Need to check node's CUDA driver and local kernel version history.
- Is there any recent model rollout / quantization push to that hostname group? (check deployment tags and PRs between 2029-10-05 00:00 and 2029-10-06 03:00)

Action items for next shift (clean handoff):
- [ ] Run full memory profiler on a drained replica (instructions in runbook but not yet tested). (owner: oncall-next)
- [ ] Coordinate with infra to run healthcheck snapshot tool once I push the quick patch. (owner: me -> infra)
- [ ] Link incident to eval job: run sample prompt set against model-variant used in region-east-1a to see cache growth pattern. (owner: applied-ml)

Notes-to-self: keep this light and timestamped. Add log snippets/grep output as attachments to INC-3279 before closing.

Misc brain-dump (less formal):
- Think about TTLing large KV entries on write if > X tokens. Might be okay to evict older context for low-traffic sessions.
- If pattern persists, consider a periodic aggressive cache compaction job during low-traffic windows.

End of shift quick checklist:
- [x] escalate to platform lead
- [x] scale fallback pool (temporary)
- [x] created INC-3279 skeleton
- [ ] follow up with postmortem template (next 24h)

-- Marta L. (dawn watch)
